scenes.title: The research problem
scenes.narration: Hello, I’m Weibing Wang. This is ReproScout, a scientific reproduction review tool I developed for MIT one point one two five. When a research program finishes, I still need to ask: did it run the original computation, and does its output actually support the answer?
scenes.visual: Open on the ReproScout title, then show the real workspace overview. Add the project name, author, and course in a restrained title card.
scenes.production_note: Use the authenticated pilot at localhost:8780. Crop or clearly label the development-host address; do not replace it with a fictional public URL.

scenes.title: What goes in and what comes out
scenes.narration: ReproScout connects those questions in one workflow. The input is a prepared project containing original code, data or documented data sources, research questions, and a pinned software environment. The output is a retained execution record, answers linked to evidence, and a portable report that another researcher can inspect.
scenes.visual: Show a simple three-part graphic: Prepared project → Original-code execution → Evidence and reviewed report. Transition into the Projects view.
scenes.on_screen_text: Original code + data + questions + environment → Evidence + review + report
scenes.production_note: The diabetes data comes from the pinned scikit-learn installation. Do not claim that every project includes a separate uploaded dataset.

scenes.title: Import the real example
scenes.narration: Here, I’m using an unchanged diabetes regression example from scikit-learn. After signing in, I upload its prepared project bundle. The app checks the archive and the input file hashes before registering it. The server needs an approved runtime. Importing a repository does not automatically resolve its dependencies.
scenes.visual: Show the signed-in Projects screen, open Import project, select the supplied example ZIP, and show successful registration in a fresh demonstration account.
scenes.on_screen_text: Prepared ZIP | Input hashes verified | Approved runtime
scenes.production_note: Do not show the access code. The existing account already contains this project; duplicate import will fail. Use a new demonstration account or explicitly label retained import footage.

scenes.title: Run with explicit limits
scenes.narration: Next, I choose the questions and set the execution limits. The controller runs the author’s code in an isolated Docker environment with networking disabled inside the scientific container. The interface keeps the run visible while it works, including partial results or failures when a task cannot finish.
scenes.visual: Open New run. Show the three questions and the model-cost cap. Start only when capturing a new authorized demonstration attempt; otherwise use retained run footage and a labeled transition.
scenes.on_screen_text: Original-code execution | Offline scientific container | Explicit budget
scenes.production_note: If waiting is shortened, display “Waiting shortened.” Never animate a fake success state or splice a different run’s cost into this run.

scenes.title: Read the actual result
scenes.narration: The recorded browser acceptance run finished in about twenty seconds, using five model calls and an estimated model cost of less than one cent. It produced a regression coefficient, a test mean squared error, and an R-squared value. Those numbers are candidate answers. Completing execution does not, by itself, establish scientific correctness.
scenes.visual: Open the retained authenticated acceptance run. Show Completed, approximately 20 seconds, 5 model calls, and the estimated model charge. Briefly reveal the three question tabs.
scenes.production_note: Use run 20261119T052436478104Z-sklearn-diabetes-ols-102-run-A1 for these figures. Exact estimated model charge: $0.00422805. Excludes hosting and image costs.

scenes.title: Inspect the evidence
scenes.narration: This is a central interaction. For the mean squared error question, I open the cited execution output. The highlighted line explicitly reports mean squared error: two thousand five hundred forty-eight point zero seven. I can check the metric name, the value, and the context, rather than trusting a generated sentence. The source integrity view shows whether any of the listed original input files were modified.
scenes.visual: Select Q2. Hold on stdout line 3 and candidate 2548.07. Slowly highlight the metric label and exact citation. Switch to Source integrity and show four unchanged inventoried files.
scenes.production_note: Keep text readable. Do not claim hashes prove semantic correctness or verify all dependencies. The retained source audit covers four prepared inputs.

scenes.title: Record a review
scenes.narration: A review records a decision, an explanation, and the evidence used to support it. Reviews also preserve the reviewer’s identity and whether the reviewer is a human or an assistant. In this recorded walkthrough, the three saved decisions are assistant reviews, not independent human validation. Earlier review versions remain available.
scenes.visual: Return to Results & review. Show a saved rationale, “assistant review by researcher,” and review history. For a new review capture, choose AI assistant and retain the new version.
scenes.production_note: Do not change the existing assistant attribution to Human for the video. Saved decisions are evidence about the walkthrough, not a completed independent usability study.

scenes.title: Export and share
scenes.narration: Finally, I export the report and open it outside the application. The package preserves the answers, evidence, and review records together. Following a citation takes me to the relevant output lines. A collaborator can examine how a conclusion was reached, instead of receiving only a final number or a screenshot.
scenes.visual: Click Export report, show the downloaded ZIP, then open the extracted report.html in a separate browser window. Click a citation and hold on the highlighted line.
scenes.on_screen_text: Portable report | Retained evidence | Traceable decisions
scenes.production_note: Use the actual exported report. Keep download paths free of unrelated personal information. Record the offline citation jump, not just the ZIP icon.

scenes.title: Show what has been validated
scenes.narration: I have also tested this fixed example successfully with GitHub Actions, using the actual Docker environment and reproduction controller. That is an integration test, not a replacement for an online execution service. The public website currently presents retained evidence. The authenticated app has been verified on the development host.
scenes.visual: Show the successful Docker reproduction acceptance workflow, then a short status card with two columns: Public evidence website and Authenticated execution pilot.
scenes.on_screen_text: GitHub CI passed | Public archive live | Public execution deployment pending
scenes.production_note: GitHub run 44469346488 is a separate attempt: 96-second full job, 17.51-second controller time. Do not merge those timings with the 20.4-second browser run.

scenes.title: Close on the product
scenes.narration: My goal is to make scientific reproduction easier to examine. Preserve the original computation, expose the evidence, and record the reviewer’s judgment. The next milestone is deploying the authenticated workflow on a suitable host and evaluating it with independent researchers. Thank you for watching.
scenes.visual: Return to a clean evidence view, then fade into a closing card with the public website and repository. Hold the final card for at least three seconds.
